audit_answers.a_run_engine_monitor_rolling_series: The rolling-history curve is folded by the PRODUCER (pipeline._run_engine_monitor_json globs ALL run_engine_monitor_*.json each run). Deleting old monitors would reset the monitor's rolling per-line history → never-delete.
audit_answers.b_brier_curve: compute_rolling_brier recomputes the full trailing-window series from predictions_history EACH RUN and embeds it in model_monitor_<date>.json; the standalone rolling_brier_<date>.json is a newest-only snapshot never read back → 2d window.
audit_answers.c_monitor_drift_coverage: Model Monitor renders drift/coverage/brier from INSIDE the newest model_monitor_<date>.json (feature_drift / feature_coverage / features_metadata / rolling_brier keys); markets page reads the run-engine dated CSVs for the resolved (newest) date. No recent-dates series tables across dated files → newest-only.
audit_answers.d_board_navigator: available_dates = todays_games_* names (remote+local) ∪ newest calibration daily[] ∪ newest predictions_history game_dates. Selecting a past date fetches todays_games_<date>.csv, shap_game_<date>_*.csv, run_engine_markets_<date>, etc. Full-fidelity reach ≈ 3 days (todays_games/shap slate window); board-backed retention keeps run-engine/predictions data for any date whose todays_games board is still tracked, so navigation never loses the RUN ENGINE block while the board exists.
audit_answers.e_pbp_defense_consumers: No production (frontend or daily-pipeline) consumer reads pbp_defense_*. The only readers are the defense ablation harnesses, which GLOB ALL dated files (research series). Per guardrail 1: exempt (never-delete), not forced into newest-1.

policy_table.source: mlb-backend/backend/retention_policy.py (FAMILY_POLICY — the single config master_pipeline Phase 6 derives from)
guardrail_notes: Allowlist is asserted disjoint from the never-delete set (test_cleanup_fix.TestRetentionPolicyConfig).

Run-dated harness OUTPUTS (calibration_ablation_*, calibration_flip_*, run_*_ablation_*.json) intentionally keep riding the date gate — the existing test_cleanup_fix pins that convention; they are regenerable run outputs, not decision records. New decision/diagnostic records should use mlb_* or *_triage_* naming to inherit protection.

step2_implementation.mechanism: Deletion lives in the git-commit path, not the untracked sweep: master_pipeline Phase 5 pushes this run's new artifacts first; Phase 6 then computes the keep-set from retention_policy.classify_artifact over `git ls-files`, `git rm`s the expired allowlisted files, commits, and pushes. Atomicity guarantee: deletions never precede the new artifacts being committed (Phase 5 push must confirm before Phase 6 runs).
changes: NEW mlb-backend/backend/retention_policy.py — the explicit policy config (FAMILY_POLICY table, EXACT_MASTER_NAMES, SERIES_PREFIXES, RECORD_PREFIXES, is_never_delete / classify_artifact / is_allowlisted).

REFACTOR mlb-backend/backend/master_pipeline.py Phase 6 — constants + predicate replaced by imports from retention_policy (no hard-coded family tuples remain). Adds two protections absent before: mlb_* + *_triage_* record prefixes, and game_level_features.csv as an exact-name master.

TESTS mlb-backend/backend/test_cleanup_fix.py — the fixture helpers now run the production predicate (retention_policy.classify_artifact); added TestRetentionPolicyConfig (family coverage, allowlist disjoint from never-delete, windows parse, series exempt), TestRetentionPolicyDryRun (exact delete list on current inventory + hermetic fixture, no non-allowlisted selection, newest-per-family survives), and master/record protection tests.

Untracked scratch (ablation_defense_*_oof.parquet, rf_study.db, etc.) never enters Phase 6 (ls-files only) — nothing to do.
